source_text: Ἀλλ’ ὡς κατὰ καιρὸν ἥκει τὸ κήρυγμα νῦν, οὕτως κατὰ καιρὸν ἐδόθη νόμος μὲν καὶ προφῆται βαρβάροις, φιλοσοφία δὲ Ἕλλησι, τὰς ἀκοὰς ἐθίζουσα πρὸς τὸ κήρυγμα. λέγει γοῦν κύριος ὁ ῥυσάμενος Ἰσραήλ· καιρῷ δεκτῷ ἐπήκουσά σου καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σωτηρίας ἐβοήθησά σοι, ἔδωκά σε εἰς διαθήκην ἐθνῶν τοῦ κατασκηνῶσαι τὴν γῆν καὶ κληρονομῆσαι κληρονομίαν ἐρήμου, λέγοντα τοῖς ἐν δεσμοῖς· ἐξέλθετε, καὶ τοῖς ἐν τῷ σκότει ἀνακαλυφθῆναι. εἰ γὰρ δέσμιοι μὲν Ἰουδαῖοι, ἐφ’ ὧν καὶ ὁ κύριος ἐξέλθετε εἶπεν ἐκ τῶν δεσμῶν οἱ θέλοντες, τοὺς ἑκουσίως δεδεμένους καὶ τὰ δυσβάστακτα φορτία (φησὶν) αὑτοῖς διὰ τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης παρεγχειρήσεως ἐπαναθεμένους λέγων, δῆλον ὡς οἱ ἐν σκότει οὗτοι ἂν εἶεν οἱ ἐν τῇ εἰδωλολατρείᾳ κατορωρυγμένον ἔχοντες τὸ ἡγεμονικόν. τοῖς μὲν γὰρ κατὰ νόμον δικαίοις ἔλειπεν ἡ πίστις, διὸ καὶ τούτους ἰώμενος ὁ κύριος ἔλεγεν· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· τοῖς δὲ κατὰ φιλοσοφίαν δικαίοις οὐχ ἡ πίστις μόνον ἡ εἰς τὸν κύριον, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ἀποστῆναι τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας ἔλειπεν. αὐτίκα ἀποκαλυφθείσης τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς προπεπραγμένοις μεταμέλονται· διόπερ ὁ κύριος εὐηγγελίσατο καὶ τοῖς ἐν Ἅιδου. φησὶ γοῦν ἡ γραφή· λέγει ὁ Ἅιδης τῇ ἀπωλείᾳ· εἶδος μὲν αὐτοῦ οὐκ εἴδομεν, φωνὴν δὲ αὐτοῦ ἠκούσαμεν. οὐχ ὁ τόπος δή που φωνὴν λαβὼν εἶπεν τὰ προειρημένα, ἀλλ’ οἱ ἐν Ἅιδου καταταγέντες καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ἑαυτοὺς ἐκδεδωκότες καθάπερ ἔκ τινος νεὼς εἰς θάλασσαν ἑκόντες ἀπορρίψαντες, οὗτοι τοίνυν εἰσὶν οἱ ἐπακούσαντες τῆς θείας δυνάμεώς τε καὶ φωνῆς· ἐπεὶ τίς ἂν εὖ φρονῶν ἐν μιᾷ καταδίκῃ καὶ τὰς τῶν δικαίων καὶ τὰς τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν ὑπολάβοι εἶναι ψυχάς, ἀδικίαν τῆς προνοίας καταχέων; τί δ’; οὐχὶ δηλοῦσιν εὐηγγελίσθαι τὸν κύριον τοῖς τε ἀπολωλόσιν ἐν τῷ κατακλυσμῷ, μᾶλλον δὲ πεπεδημένοις, καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ τε καὶ φρουρᾷ συνεχομένοις; δέδεικται δὲ κάν τῷ δευτέρῳ Στρωματεῖ τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἀκολούθως τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ τοὺς ἐν Ἅιδου εὐηγγελισμένους· ἐχρῆν γάρ, οἶμαι, ὥσπερ κἀνταῦθα, οὕτως δὲ κἀκεῖσε τοὺς ἀρίστους τῶν μαθητῶν μιμητὰς γενέσθαι τοῦ διδασκάλου, ἵν’ ὃ μὲν τοὺς ἐξ Ἑβραίων, οἳ δὲ τὰ ἔθνη εἰς ἐπιστροφὴν ἀγάγωσι, τουτέστιν τοὺς ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ τῇ κατὰ νόμον καὶ κατὰ φιλοσοφίαν βεβιωκότας μέν, οὐ τελείως δέ, ἀλλ’ ἁμαρτητικῶς διαπεραναμένους τὸν βίον·
pass_a_gloss: But as the preaching came in due time, so also the law was given in due time to the barbarians and prophets to the Greeks and philosophy to the Greeks, training their ears for the preaching. For the Lord who redeemed Israel says: In an acceptable time I listened to you and on the day of salvation I helped you, I gave you as a covenant to the nations to inhabit the earth and to inherit the inheritance of the desert, saying to those in bonds: Come out, and to those in darkness: Be revealed. For if the Jews are prisoners, and the Lord said to them Come out of the bonds those who want, those who voluntarily bound themselves and the unbearable burdens (he says) they placed on themselves through human effort, saying, it is clear that those in darkness are those who have idolatry rooted in them having the ruling power. For those who are righteous according to the law, faith was lacking, therefore the Lord also healed them saying: Your faith has saved you; for those who are righteous according to philosophy, not only faith in the Lord was lacking, but also to turn away from idolatry. As soon as the truth was revealed, they also repented for what they had done; therefore the Lord preached the gospel to those in Hades. For the scripture says: Hades says to destruction: We have not seen his form, but we have heard his voice. It was not the place that received the voice and said the aforementioned things, but those who were led into Hades and gave themselves over to destruction, as if they had willingly thrown themselves from a ship into the sea, these are the ones who heard the divine power and voice; for who would think that in one condemnation the souls of the righteous and the unrighteous are together, pouring injustice on the providence? What then? Does it not show that the Lord preached the gospel to those who were lost in the flood, or rather those who were bound, and to those who were held in prison and guard? But it has been shown also in the second Stromata that the apostles, following the Lord, also preached the gospel to those in Hades; for it was necessary, I think, that just as here, so also there, the best of the disciples would become imitators of the teacher, so that he might lead the ones from the Hebrews, and they might lead the nations to repentance, that is, those who lived in righteousness according to the law and according to philosophy, but not perfectly, but sinfully passing through life;

bible_refs.note: In an acceptable time I listened to you
He sent his word and healed them
He preached to the spirits in prison

pass_b_english: Just as the preaching arrived at the appointed moment, so the law and the prophets were given in their season to the barbarians, and philosophy to the Greeks, to prepare their hearing for the gospel. The Lord who redeemed Israel declares: "In an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you; I gave you as a covenant to the nations, to establish the earth and to inherit the desolate heritages," saying to the prisoners, "Come out," and to those in darkness, "Be revealed" (Isaiah 49:8). If the Jews are the prisoners to whom the Lord said, "Come out of the bonds," then the ones who want to leave are those who bound themselves voluntarily and loaded themselves with unbearable burdens through human contrivance; clearly, those in darkness are the ones who have idolatry rooted in their governing faculty. For those who were righteous according to the law lacked faith, so the Lord healed them as well, saying, "Your faith has saved you"; but for those who were righteous according to philosophy, not only was faith in the Lord lacking, but also the turning away from idolatry. The moment the truth was disclosed, they too repented of their former deeds; therefore the Lord preached the gospel even to those in Hades. Scripture says: "Hades says to Destruction, 'We have not seen his form, but we have heard his voice'" (Psalm 107:20). It was not the place itself that received a voice and spoke those words, but the souls consigned to Hades who gave themselves over to destruction — like men who willingly throw themselves from a ship into the sea — and these are the ones who heard the divine power and voice. Who in their right mind would suppose that in a single condemnation the souls of the righteous and the wicked are lumped together, charging providence with injustice? What then? Does this not show that the Lord preached the gospel to those lost in the flood — or rather, to those who were bound — and to those held in prison and under guard (1 Peter 3:19)? It has also been demonstrated in the second Stromata that the apostles, following the Lord, preached the gospel to those in Hades as well; for it was necessary, I think, that just as the best disciples imitated the Teacher here, so they would do the same there, so that some would bring the Hebrews and others the nations to repentance — that is, those who had lived righteously according to the law and according to philosophy, yet not perfectly, but who passed through life in a sinful manner.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version with appropriate scripture identifications (Isaiah 49:8, Psalm 107:20, 1 Peter 3:19) which are required for clarity in patristic contexts. All clauses, including the complex discussion on the 'ruling power' (ἡγεμονικόν) and the distinction between the Jews and the nations, are preserved.
